inputs.share_count_basis: 587,107,850 ordinary shares at 31-Mar-2026; basic and diluted EPS identical (HK$3.48), no share-option or share-award scheme expensed. Held flat; no buybacks in any year FY2018-FY2026.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report (Annual_FY2025.txt, year ended 31-Mar-2026): no share-based payment line in the cash-flow statement or notes; EquityAwardTaxes 0 every period. SBC-zero market.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z (HKEX regular close, Friday; Yahoo chart API)
inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD is pegged to USD, so the discount rate is built on USD/HKD rates: risk-free 4.0% (HKD/USD 10y blend), ERP 6.0% for a HK/Mainland consumer-discretionary exposure, beta ~0.95 -> cost of equity ~9.7%; debt (bank loans + gold loans, ~12% of capital at market) at ~4% pre-tax / 3.3% after tax -> WACC ~9.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: gold-price and Mainland-consumer risk is charged in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not again in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: the full lease payment (FY2026 HK$424.9m 'Repayment of lease liabilities (including interest)', financing section) is charged as lease_cost_pct (~2.5% of revenue) inside EBIT; lease liabilities (HK$555.9m) are EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (PPE 142.0 + investment property 29.2 + intangibles 33.0 = 204.3m, 1.2% of revenue), so the lease is charged once. FY2026 check: EBITDA 18.9% - lease 2.5% - D&A 1.2% = 15.2% vs reported operating margin 15.4%.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of 3DG, 71% owned). The 29% 3DG minority is charged once, in equity_bridge (HK$200m, ~7x a mid-cycle ~HK$29m/yr NCI profit share). NCI book value is negative (-HK$90m) and FY2026 NCI share of profit was a HK$30m loss, so nothing is deducted in the flows.
inputs.gold_loans_treatment: Gold loans (HK$1,970.5m, cash-settled, marked to gold) are included in total_debt alongside bank borrowings (HK$2,224.6m), matching the company's own net-borrowing definition (HK$1,834m). They economically hedge ~25-30% of gold inventory, which sits in operating working capital; the inventory is not added to the bridge (it is needed to trade).
inputs.working_capital_note: Inventory is the business: HK$14,617m at 31-Mar-2026 = 85% of revenue, 503 closing turnover days, and it re-prices with gold. wc_capture -75% of the revenue change in every scenario (inventory ~0.85x revenue less a small payables offset). History confirms the drain: FY2019-FY2026 inventory rose HK$5.3bn (ex-3DG acquisition ~0.6bn) on only +HK$1.3bn of revenue, because gold inflation lifts inventory cost while volumes fell. Reported FCF is therefore far below net income in rising-gold years (FY2026 OCF HK$23m vs NPAT HK$2,046m).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF + non-US/cyclical adaptations (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'). Luk Fook is an operating retailer/wholesaler/licensor, not a financial, REIT or holdco; first valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry, no prior DCF). FILENAME TRAP: Extracted/0590.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt is the FY2026 report (year ended 31-Mar-2026); filenames run one fiscal year behind the period labels in core_metrics. PEAK-YEAR NORMALISATION: FY2026 is a record year (gold +50% YoY, gross margin 36.7%, operating margin 15.4% even after HK$840m of hedging losses on gold loans and derivatives). The base case does NOT carry it forward: EBIT margin glides 14.8% FY2027 (Citi ~flat FY2027 profit; management's double-digit growth guidance treated as bull) to a 12.5% mid-cycle, against a FY2018-FY2026 average of 12.7% and a FY2025 trough of 10.6%. Revenue base FY2026 HK$17,205m is itself gold-inflated, so base growth is 6% then a flat FY2028 (gold normalises) before ~3% nominal. Interest income (HK$18m) is NOT stripped: the company is net-debt (HK$1,834m), so no cash pile is double-counted. Owner FCF FY0 = reported FCF (OCF 23.2 - capex 101.7 = -78.5) - lease payments 424.9 = -503.4; it is NOT a base for the projection (the component build from revenue is), and is negative because of the gold-driven HK$3.9bn inventory build. SBC-zero: house and street coincide, band_position null. Buybacks zero; the flat count is genuine (no issuance). Capex 1.4% of revenue: FY2018-FY2026 average 2.2% includes lumpy shop-property purchases (FY2019 HK$887m, FY2024 HK$676m); maintenance ~0.8%; 1.4% allows for periodic property buys plus overseas shop roll-out. Investment properties (HK$772m book) are NOT added to the bridge because their rental income sits in other income inside operating profit (matching-asset rule). Cash tax 21% (effective 21.8% FY2026; HK 16.5% / Mainland 25% / Macao 12% blend); FY2026 cash tax paid (HK$359m) lagged the provision (HK$563m), so a part of FY2027's cash tax catches up - not modelled separately. Terminal cap 12x (cyclical consumer). TERMINAL: the 12x cap binds in all three scenarios (Gordon at 9.0%/2.5% would be ~15.8x), so the WACC x g grid is flat across terminal growth; the value is sensitive to WACC, the mid-cycle margin and wc_capture, not to g. BEAR DESTOCKING: with wc_capture symmetric, the bear's FY2027-28 revenue decline releases ~HK$1.9bn of inventory cash (~HK$3/share PV); this is historically grounded - FY2020-21 (revenue -29%/-21%) inventory fell HK$2.0bn and owner FCF was HK$2.4bn/HK$1.9bn, the best years in the series.

equity_bridge.note: Luk Fook owns 71% (FY2026 AR subsidiaries note, line 12194); ~7x a mid-cycle HK$29m/yr minority profit share. Charged here only; flows are consolidated.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 5.8% vs revenue 14.2% and EPS 15.0%: >30% divergence. The 5yr window starts at the COVID trough (FY2021 revenue HK$8.9bn) and ends at a gold-price peak, so revenue/EPS CAGRs are cycle artefacts; the through-cycle FY2018-FY2026 revenue CAGR is only 2.1%. Equity CAGR (after a ~45-60% payout) is the more representative compounding rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (OCF - capex - lease payments): FY2020 2,397; FY2021 1,905; FY2022 -112; FY2023 940; FY2024 643; FY2025 366; FY2026 -503 (HK$m). No SBC or interest-income adjustment applies (SBC-zero; net debt). FCF CAGRs are undefined (negative end point); the series averages ~HK$805m/yr FY2020-FY2026 against average NPAT ~HK$1.4bn because rising gold prices kept absorbing cash into inventory.

base.narrative: Gold stays elevated but stops rising; FY2027 revenue +6% on strong early trading (HK/Macao SSS >40%, Mainland >20% to 21-Jun-2026) and profit roughly flat (Citi ~+0.8%) as holding gains on fixed-price product fade; FY2028 flat as gold normalises; then ~3% nominal growth from overseas shops, 3DG and fixed-price mix offsetting Mainland franchise attrition. EBIT margin settles at 12.5%, just below the FY2018-26 average, reflecting the Nov-2025 Mainland VAT cost increase.

bull.narrative: Management's double-digit FY2027 growth is delivered: gold holds its highs, the VAT-driven Mainland-to-HK/Macao price gap keeps tourists buying in Luk Fook's self-operated HK/Macao shops, fixed-price/gem-set mix (38% GM) keeps rising, 3DG becomes a real second engine and the overseas plan (+30 shops, 2 new countries in FY2027) compounds. EBIT margin holds ~14.5%, near FY2026's record ex-holding-gains.

bear.narrative: Gold retraces from its January-2026 highs, deflating weight-based revenue (~66% of sales) and leaving a high-cost 503-day inventory to sell through at compressed margin; Mainland consumer stays weak and franchise closures (-282 shops in FY2026) continue; the VAT cost increase is absorbed. Revenue -10% then -5%, EBIT margin back to the FY2025 trough (~10.5%) recovering only to ~11%. Lease costs are sticky, so they rise as a share of revenue. Inventory destocking releases some cash in the first two years.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle normalisation from a gold-price peak: FY2027 revenue +6% with profit ~flat, FY2028 flat, then ~3% nominal growth; EBIT margin 14.8% -> 12.5% (FY2018-26 average 12.7%). Gold inventory reinvestment (75% of every revenue dollar added) keeps owner FCF well below net income.
scenario_narratives.bull: Gold stays high and the VAT-driven tourist shift, fixed-price mix and 3DG/overseas growth deliver management's double-digit guidance; revenue +12% FY2027, ~4-5% thereafter, EBIT margin ~14.5% sustained.
scenario_narratives.bear: Gold retraces and Mainland stays weak: revenue -10% / -5% in FY2027-28, margins back to the FY2025 trough (~10.5-11% EBIT), sticky store leases, continued franchise attrition.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because FY2026 is a record, gold-inflated peak and ~66% of sales re-price with a commodity that has already pulled back from its highs (the stock is -35% from its 52-week high). Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs gold to stay high AND Mainland demand to hold AND the overseas/3DG plans to execute. Base 50% is the sell-side-consistent flat-FY2027 path with mid-cycle margins.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A gold retailer's reported earnings overstate owner cash flow whenever gold rises, because the inventory (85% of revenue, ~500 days) must be refinanced at higher prices. The model values Luk Fook on a mid-cycle margin with that inventory reinvestment charged explicitly, leases charged as an operating cost, and gold loans treated as debt, rather than on FY2026's peak profit.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gold price direction: drives revenue, gross margin (holding gains/losses on fixed-price stock) and hedging gains/losses (HK$840m net loss in FY2026) simultaneously
Working-capital capture: a -75% capture on revenue growth is the single largest driver of owner FCF; a more inventory-light model (or faster turns) would lift value materially
Mainland franchise attrition and the Nov-2025 VAT reform on Mainland jewellery margins
HK/Macao tourist flows and per-capita spend
Leverage: bank + gold loans rose 91% in FY2026 to HK$4.2bn to fund inventory
